profile.reading: This building is one of three data centers on Vantage Data Centers' Quincy, Washington campus at 2101 M Street NE, in Grant County on the Columbia River plateau. Vantage bought into the Quincy market because Grant County Public Utility District sells some of the lowest-cost hydroelectric power in the continental United States, drawn from the Wanapum and Priest Rapids dams on the Columbia River, a locational advantage that also drew Microsoft, Yahoo, Sabey, and Intuit data centers to the same small city. The full Quincy campus covers roughly 68 acres and totals about 775,000 square feet across its three buildings, with a combined critical IT load Vantage has stated at approximately 89 megawatts. Vantage's own campus materials name WA11 individually, citing Uptime Institute Tier III Design and Constructed certification, Tier III Gold Operational Sustainability status, and LEED Gold; the operator's public materials do not break out WA12 and WA13 by name, certification, or individual square footage and megawatt figures the way WA11 is described, so this facility's own specifications should be read as part of the shared campus totals rather than an individually confirmed number. Design follows Vantage's standard N+1 mechanical redundancy approach, with diesel generators meeting current EPA Tier II emissions standards for backup power, and the region's cool, dry high-desert climate supports significant use of outside air for cooling, reducing water and mechanical-cooling load compared with humid climates. Grant County's data center cluster has drawn periodic scrutiny over discounted industrial power rates for large users versus residential ratepayers, a recurring subject in Grant County PUD commission meetings and in Washington state legislative discussion of data center electricity consumption. Quincy's data center campuses, including Vantage's, sit within Grant County's designated industrial and manufacturing zoning, and the city has continued to permit expansion of the sector as a significant local employer and tax base contributor for a town of roughly 8,000 residents.

reading.body:
Vantage WA12 is one of three buildings on a Vantage campus in Quincy, Washington that publishes 89 MW of critical IT load across 775,000 square feet total. The individual building's capacity is not published separately. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, the full campus would accommodate roughly 2,200 racks, though the actual mix and density at this site are unknown.

This campus ranks third by published capacity in Washington state, behind two other facilities. Washington has 46 mapped data centers total but only three with published megawatt figures from operator spec pages, of which this campus represents the third-largest share of the 60 MW total published for the state.

No certifications, power source details, or grid connection specifics are published for this facility. The research status is complete, meaning no additional published specifications for WA12 exist beyond the three-building campus totals.
